# Line-coverage floor for the `coverage-integration` CI job, in per cent.
#
# Enforced by `cargo run -p xtask -- coverage-ratchet --integration`. One number, or the word
# `unset`; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored.
#
# NOT the same number as `.github/coverage-floor.txt`, and never interchangeable with it. That
# file is the floor on the *offline* suite. This one is the floor on
# `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets --features integration`, which additionally runs the
# 118 `crates/db`, 86 `services/api` and 55 `services/sync` tests that need Docker — where the
# bulk of this repository's real coverage lives. Expect this number to be substantially higher
# than the offline one; copying a value from one file into the other produces either a gate that
# can never pass or a gate that can never fail.
#
# WHAT IT MEASURES. The whole host workspace, every target, with the `integration` feature on, so
# a regression in code only the Docker-backed suites reach moves this number. It moves nothing in
# the offline floor, which is the blind spot this file exists to close.
#
# WHEN TO LOWER IT. Only when code was deleted, or a suite was deliberately retired. The offline
# floor's one legitimate reason — "the drop is code the integration suites cover" — has no
# counterpart here, because this measurement *is* those suites.
#
# WHEN TO RAISE IT. Whenever the measured value has drifted a couple of points above it. The job
# prints the headroom and suggests a new value once there is enough, and writes both to the run
# summary. A ratchet that only ever holds its original line stops being a ratchet.
#
# `unset` IS THE STARTING STATE, and the only non-numeric value accepted. While it is set the job
# measures, prints what it found and enforces nothing; every other word is a parse error, so the
# gate cannot be switched off by a typo. The sentinel is here because this measurement costs a
# Docker Postgres, the migrations and an instrumented build of the whole workspace — nobody can
# take it on a laptop in the time a change deserves, so the first value has to come from a real
# CI run rather than from a guess. Replace the line below with what that run prints (it suggests
# a value about a point under the measurement, absorbing `proptest`'s entropy-seeded runs), and
# record the date and the measured figure here the way `.github/coverage-floor.txt` does.
#
# Only the `full` path measures this: the weekly `schedule` run, or `workflow_dispatch` with the
# `full` input. So unlike the offline floor, editing this file does not re-measure it on a pull
# request — the run that fills the sentinel in is the one that has to be read.
unset
